## Introduction
During the previous step I filtered out 5 bad quality samples(4 were H2O control samples), now I want to remove the bad quality probes. This is important because can cause artifacts in the data and problems in the downstream analysis. 

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, dev = "CairoPNG")
```

### Load packages

```{r warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(minfi)
library(tidyverse)
```

### Qc metrics for probes quality check
- Detection pvalues probe-wise, remove probes with detection p-values > 0.05 i.e > 25% of total samples.
- Remove cross reactive probes, these cr probes are identified in literature.
- Remove probes containing SNPs within 3 nucleotides of the CpG site and MAF > 10%.
- Exclude probes from X and Y chromosomes? To avoid spurious methylation differences. Check this paper: https://epigeneticsandchromatin.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s13072-022-00477-0
- Remove High intensity probes
- Remove probes with more than 5% of the samples having low bead numbers (<3).

### Load sample filtered objects
```{r}
load("../../results/01_pre_process/02_sample_QC/SetObjects/sf_rgSet_ext.RData")
load("../../results/01_pre_process/02_sample_QC/SetObjects/sf_MSet.RData")
load("../../results/01_pre_process/02_sample_QC/SetObjects/sf_grSet.RData")
```

# Keep CpGs starting with cg

```{r}
dim(sf.MSet)
cg.sf.MSet <- sf.MSet[grepl("^cg", rownames(sf.MSet)), ]
dim(cg.sf.MSet)

failed.probes1 <- minfi::featureNames(sf.MSet)[
  !minfi::featureNames(sf.MSet) %in% minfi::featureNames(cg.sf.MSet)]

length(failed.probes1)
```

### Probe-wise detection p-value
The same as for samples, we want to remove probes showing detection p-values (e.g >0.05). For example the scanner can failed to read signals from some probes due to low intensities or artifacts in the array.

The way that computational methods deal with this is by comparing the signal of a certain probe to the average signal from the negative controls.
```{r}
# ensure probes are in the same order in the mSetSq and detP objects
detP <- detectionP(sf.rgSet_ext)
detP <- detP[match(featureNames(sf.MSet), rownames(detP)),]

# remove any probes that have failed in one or more samples; this next line
# checks for each row of detP whether the number of values < 0.01 is equal
# to the number of samples (TRUE) or not (FALSE)
keep <- rowSums(detP < 0.01) == ncol(sf.MSet)
table(keep)

sf.MSet.detP <- sf.MSet[keep,]

failed.probes2 <- minfi::featureNames(sf.MSet)[
  !minfi::featureNames(sf.MSet) %in% minfi::featureNames(sf.MSet.detP)]

length(failed.probes2)
```
### Remove cross-reactive probes
I used the following package https://github.com/markgene/maxprobes for EPIC/850k cross-reactive probes correction.

**Note: ** "6% of the array probes can potentially generate spurious signals because of co-hybridization to alternate genomic sequences highly homologous to the intended targets." as written in the paper below:
https://genomebiology.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s13059-016-1066-1


```{r warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(maxprobes)
cr_EPIC = maxprobes::xreactive_probes(array_type = "EPIC")
cr_EPIC_pedsley = read_csv(
  "../../docs/probes/Technical_probes_TS1-13059_2016_1066_MOESM1_ESM.csv"
  )

print(dim(sf.MSet))
MsetEx_noXloci <- maxprobes::dropXreactiveLoci(sf.MSet)

diff = length(sf.MSet@NAMES) - length(MsetEx_noXloci@NAMES)

print(paste0("Number of cr probes in function: " , length(cr_EPIC)))
print(paste0("Number of cr probes from Pedsley et al: ",dim(cr_EPIC_pedsley)[1]))
print(paste0("CpGs in sample filtered MSet: ", length(sf.MSet@NAMES)))
print(paste0("CpGs in samples and cr probes filtered in MSet: ", length(MsetEx_noXloci@NAMES)))
print(paste0("Number of cr probes removed: " , diff))

```

```{r}
MsetEx_noXloci
```

### Cross-reactive probes to remove
The sf.MSet have a total number of probes equal to 866238, after dropping reactive probes, I get MsetEx_noXloci = 823015 probes. 
In total were removed 43223 reactive probes. Which is expected for EPIC/850k array.

```{r}
# Find cross reactive probes
failed.probes3 <- minfi::featureNames(sf.MSet)[
  !minfi::featureNames(sf.MSet) %in% minfi::featureNames(MsetEx_noXloci)
]

length(failed.probes3)
```

### Remove probes containing SNPs
I want to remove those snps within 3 nucleotides of the CpG site and MAF > 1%.
Look at this post for better understanding.

https://support.bioconductor.org/p/9155604/#9155624

```{r}
dim(sf.grSet)
all.probes <- rownames(sf.grSet)

sf.grSet.nosnp <- dropLociWithSnps(
                        sf.grSet,
                        snps = c("CpG", "SBE"),
                        maf = 0 # remove any snp 
                        )

nosnp.probes <- rownames(sf.grSet.nosnp)

failed.probes4 <- all.probes[!(all.probes %in% nosnp.probes)]
length(failed.probes4)
```

### Exclude probes from X and Y chromosomes
#### Remove directly all probes in chrX and chrY. 

```{r}
ann850k <- minfi::getAnnotation(IlluminaHumanMethylationEPICanno.ilm10b4.hg19)

xy.probes <- rownames(ann850k)[which(ann850k$chr=="chrX" | ann850k$chr=="chrY")]
sf.MSet.filt.xy <- sf.MSet[rownames(sf.MSet) %in% xy.probes, ]

failed.probes5 <- rownames(sf.MSet.filt.xy)
length(failed.probes5)
```
### High intensity probes
From this paper: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4239800/

"For example, we have looked at the relation between signal intensities and DNA methylation measurements [b-values, defined as the ratio of the methylated signal over the total signal (methylated + unmethylated) and have observed that probes displaying a high average intensity (i.e. a high average of the methylated and unmethylated signals) are more prone than probes displaying a lower average intensity to provide DNA methylation measurements inconsistent with measurements obtained with other approaches, such as BPS (bisulfite pyrosequencing).

They have a tendency to provide values close to 0.5, independently of their true methylation state. Of note, type II Infinium probes seem to be less prone to this phenomenon."

```{r}
# Retrieve probe design info
manifest <- getManifest(sf.rgSet_ext)
snpProbesI <- getProbeInfo(manifest, type = "I")$Name

Meth <- getMeth(sf.MSet)
Unmeth <- getUnmeth(sf.MSet)
# Median
Methmed <- apply(Meth, 1, median)
Unmethmed <- apply(Unmeth, 1, median)


MUmed <- sqrt(Methmed*Unmethmed)

hist(MUmed)

# Tatiana
hi.MU <- names(which(MUmed > 10000)) # cutoff at MU = 10,000
failed.probes6 <- hi.MU[hi.MU %in% snpProbesI]
length(failed.probes6)
```


### Get probes  more than 5% of samples have bead numer below 3
**Note: the Watermelon beadcount() function work with rgSet extended object.**

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library("wateRmelon")

# Run bead count
df.bead.counts <- wateRmelon::beadcount(sf.rgSet_ext)

# Function to calculate percentage of NAs in each row (probes)
pct.of.nas <- function(row) {
  sum(is.na(row)) / length(row) * 100
}

df.bead.counts$na_pct <- apply(df.bead.counts, 1, pct.of.nas)

# Filter out probes > 5% NAs
failed.probes7 <- df.bead.counts %>% 
                        dplyr::filter(na_pct > 5) %>%
                        rownames()
length(failed.probes7)
```


### Remove all bad quality probes
] 106162
[1] "We need to discard 7119 42944 29958 19627 8675 and 6596 probes as it was pointed during the analysis."
[1] "In total we discard 106162 probes"

```{r}
out.dir <- file.path("../../results/01_pre_process/03_probes_QC/failed_probes/")

# write failed probes-files
failed.probes <- unique(
  c(failed.probes1,
    failed.probes2,
    failed.probes3,
    failed.probes4,
    failed.probes5,
    failed.probes6,
    failed.probes7
    )
  )
print(length(failed.probes))

write(
  failed.probes1,
  file = file.path(out.dir, "failed_probes1_keep_start_with_cg.txt")
)
write(
  failed.probes2,
  file = file.path(out.dir, "failed_probes2_low_detection_pvalues.txt")
)
write(
  failed.probes3,
  file = file.path(out.dir, "failed_probes3_crossreactive.txt")
)
write(
  failed.probes4,
  file = file.path(out.dir, "failed_probes4_snpsites_at_interrogation.txt")
)
write(
  failed.probes5,
  file = file.path(out.dir, "failed_probes5_xy_problematic_probes.txt")
)
write(
  failed.probes6,
  file = file.path(out.dir, "failed_probes6_high_intensity_signals.txt")
)

write(
  failed.probes7,
  file = file.path(out.dir, "failed_probes7_low_bead_counts.txt")
)


# All probes to remove
write(failed.probes, file = file.path(out.dir, "failed_probes.txt"))

# print summary data
print(
  paste(
    "We need to discard",
    length(failed.probes1),
    length(failed.probes2),
    length(failed.probes3),
    length(failed.probes4),
    length(failed.probes5),
    length(failed.probes6),
    "and",
    length(failed.probes7),
    "probes as it was pointed during the analysis."
  ),
  sep = " "
)

print(
  paste(
    "In total we discard",
    length(unique(failed.probes)),
    "probes"
  ),
  sep = " "
)
tail(failed.probes)
```

## Create density plots of failed probe sets
### A difference in the distribution of beta-values may signal a genuine problem with probes. 

```{r warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(gridExtra)
library("RColorBrewer")

palette(brewer.pal(9, 'Set1'))
out.dir.plots = file.path("../../results/01_pre_process/03_probes_QC/plots")

betas <- getBeta(sf.MSet)
all.probes <- rownames(betas)

# Plot+++++++
pdf(file.path(out.dir.plots, "density_plots_failed_probes.pdf"))
par(mfrow=c(4,2))

# Unfiltered
try(
densityPlot(betas, main = "Unfiltered probe-set") 
)
# Filtered probe-set
betas.filt <- betas[which(!(all.probes %in% failed.probes)),]
try(
densityPlot(
  betas.filt,
  main = "Filtered probe-set"
  )
)

# Probes with low detection P-values
try(
densityPlot(
  betas[which(all.probes %in% failed.probes2),],
  main = "Low detection P-value"
  )
)
# Cross-reactive
try(
densityPlot(
  betas[which(all.probes %in% failed.probes3),],
  main = "Crossreactive probes"
  ) 
)
# Probes with SNPs at interrogation / extension site at MAF = 0.1
try(
densityPlot(
  betas[which(all.probes %in% failed.probes4),],
  main = "Probes with interfering SNP-sites"
  )
)
# Probes xy problematic
try(
densityPlot(
  betas[which(all.probes %in% failed.probes5),],
  main = "XY problematic probes"
  )
)
# Type I probes with high intensity signals
try(
densityPlot(
  betas[which(all.probes %in% failed.probes6),],
  main = "High intensity signal probes"
  )
)
# Probes with low bead counts
try(
densityPlot(
  betas[which(all.probes %in% failed.probes7),],
  main = "Low bead counts"
  )
)

dev.off()
```

## Remove failed probes
### Filter MSet object
 "In total we discard 108961 probes"
I should have 757277 left

```{r}
# read list of probes for removal
rm.probes <- unique(failed.probes)
length(rm.probes)

dim(sf.MSet)
# Probe filtering
r.probes.raw <- which(rownames(sf.MSet) %in% rm.probes)
rp.sf.MSet <- sf.MSet[-r.probes.raw, ]
dim(rp.sf.MSet)

out.setObject <- file.path("../../results/01_pre_process/03_probes_QC/SetObjects/")
save(rp.sf.MSet, file = file.path(out.setObject, "rp_sf_MSet.RData"))
```


```{r}
group = rp.sf.MSet@colData$Group_detailed
group2 = rp.sf.MSet@colData$Gender
names <- rp.sf.MSet@colData$Sample_Name


mdsPlot(
  rp.sf.MSet,
  sampGroups=group2,
  sampNames = names,
  legendNCol=2,
  legendPos = "bottom"
)
```
